sheet.howExamined: C2, 1 hour 15 minutes, 70 marks at Foundation and 80 at Higher, with a calculator and the Chemistry Data Leaflet. Features of a homologous series come as a tick-three or a state-three [3]; a family is named from its general formula [1]; a formula is worked out from the general formula [1]; the definition of a hydrocarbon is [2], marked as 'consists of only' plus 'carbon and hydrogen'.

steps.working: Eth means two carbons, joined by a single bond: C–C.
steps.decision: Chain first. The prefix gives the number of carbons, and an alkane is saturated so the link is a single bond.

accepted: Eth means two carbons, joined by a single bond: C–C.

steps.working: Each carbon has used one bond, so each takes three hydrogens: 3 + 3 = 6.
steps.decision: Count to four at every carbon. Six lines to H and one line to the other carbon means four bonds on each, which is the check that your drawing is right.

options: Because every carbon atom forms exactly four bonds
Because the formula has to end in an even number
whyMenu.explain: Carbon's four bonds fix the hydrogen count; you never have to remember it separately.

steps.working: Molecular formula: C₂H₆. Check with the general formula: 2 × 2 + 2 = 6.
steps.decision: Always check a formula against CnH2n+2. It costs five seconds and catches a miscount.

accepted: Molecular formula: C₂H₆. Check with the general formula: 2 × 2 + 2 = 6.

steps.working: From the Data Leaflet, Ar(C) = 12 and Ar(H) = 1.
steps.decision: Take both relative atomic masses from the leaflet rather than memory. A wrong Ar loses the Mr mark, though later steps still follow through.

accepted: From the Data Leaflet, Ar(C) = 12 and Ar(H) = 1.

steps.decision: Multiply each Ar by how many of that atom the formula has. Adding 12 and 1 once each is the commonest slip.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: (a) Two carbons joined by a single bond, with three hydrogens on each. (b) C₂H₆. (c) Mr = 2 × 12 + 6 × 1 = 30.

steps.working: The boiling point rises as the number of carbon atoms rises.
steps.decision: Name the direction and what it depends on. A trend answer that says only 'it changes' earns nothing.

accepted: The boiling point rises as the number of carbon atoms rises.

steps.decision: Write the subtraction before you touch the calculator. Both numbers are negative, so the order matters: the other way round gives -161 °C.

accepted: Difference = butane − methane = -1 − (-162).

steps.decision: Taking away a negative number adds it on. The answer is a rise, so it must come out positive.

steps.working: Every boiling point is below 20 °C, so at room temperature all four have already boiled: they are gases.
steps.decision: Compare each value with room temperature rather than asserting the state. That comparison is the mark.

accepted: Every boiling point is below 20 °C, so at room temperature all four have already boiled: they are gases.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: (a) The boiling point rises as the chain gets longer. (b) -1 − (-162) = 161 °C. (c) All four boil below 20 °C, so at room temperature they are all gases.

options.text: four

options.text: two
options.feedback: Oxygen forms two. Carbon has four outer electrons and forms four bonds, which is why its chemistry is so rich.

options.text: six
options.feedback: Six is the number of electrons in a carbon atom altogether, not the number of bonds. It forms four.

options.text: a compound consisting of hydrogen and carbon only

options.text: a compound containing hydrogen and carbon

options.text: all four are liquids

options.text: it cannot be worked out from boiling points

items.stem: Why do the alkanes have similar chemical properties?

options.text: they contain the same kinds of bond, so they react in the same ways
options.feedback: Same bonds, same reactions. Only the chain length changes along the family.

options.text: they have the same boiling point

options.text: they all have the same number of carbons
options.feedback: The carbon count is what changes from one member to the next. The bonding is what stays the same.

options.text: they all have a functional group
options.feedback: Alkanes have no functional group, which is exactly why they are the least reactive family here.

items.stem: What does a displayed formula show that a molecular formula does not?

options.text: every bond in the molecule, drawn as a line

options.text: how many atoms of each element there are

options.text: the relative formula mass
options.feedback: Neither formula shows the Mr; you work that out from the Data Leaflet.

options.text: the state at room temperature
options.feedback: No formula shows the state. You get that from the boiling point.

parts.stem:
The first four alkanes are methane, ethane, propane and butane. The graph gives their boiling points.

indicativeContent.point: They share the general formula CnH2n+2.
Successive members differ by a CH2 group.
They show similar chemical properties, because they contain the same kinds of bond.
Their physical properties show a gradation: they change steadily from one member to the next.
The graph shows the boiling point rising steadily as the chain gets longer.
The rise is steady rather than sudden, which is what a gradation means.
All four boil below room temperature, so all four are gases.

scheme.for: a banded answer covering the four features of a homologous series and reading the gradation off the graph: the shared general formula, the CH2 step, similar chemical properties, a gradation in physical properties, the steady rise in boiling point, and all four being gases at room temperature
scheme.examinerNote: A point contradicted elsewhere in the answer is not counted. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Four features, then the evidence.
Use the graph for the physical half of the answer.
parts.workedSolution: The alkanes are a homologous series because every member has the same general formula, CnH2n+2, and successive members differ by a CH2 group. They show similar chemical properties, because each molecule contains the same kinds of bond and only the length of the chain changes. They also show a gradation in their physical properties, and the graph is the evidence for that: the boiling point rises steadily from methane to butane as each carbon is added, rather than jumping about. Every one of those boiling points is below room temperature, so all four alkanes are gases at room temperature.

context.setting: Decane, one of the alkanes in kerosene

parts.stem:
Decane is an alkane with 10 carbon atoms.
Use the general formula of the alkanes to give its molecular formula.
hints: Double the carbons, then add two.
parts.workedSolution: 2 × 10 + 2 = 22, so decane is C10H22.

parts.stem: Use the Data Leaflet to calculate the relative formula mass of decane.
hints: Multiply each relative atomic mass by the number of those atoms.

commonErrors.feedback: The hydrogens are multiplied but the carbons are not. There are 10 carbons, so the first term is 10 × 12.
The carbons are multiplied but the hydrogens are not. There are 22 of them, so add 22 × 1.

parts.stem: Calculate the percentage by mass of hydrogen in decane. Give your answer to one decimal place.
hints: The mass of hydrogen in the formula goes on top; the whole Mr goes underneath.
parts.workedSolution: (22 ÷ 142) × 100 = 15.493…, which is 15.5% to one decimal place.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the percentage of carbon. The question asks for hydrogen, so 22 × 1 goes on top.
That divides the whole by the part, the fraction upside down. A percentage of something cannot come out above 100.

parts.stem: Decane melts at −30 °C and boils at 174 °C. State its physical state at room temperature, 20 °C.

accepted: liquid

hints: Where does 20 °C sit between the melting and boiling points?
parts.workedSolution: Liquid: 20 °C is above its melting point and below its boiling point.

commonErrors.feedback: Decane boils at 174 °C, far above room temperature, so at 20 °C it has not boiled: it is a liquid.

findTheMistake.stem:
Aoife is asked: 'An alkane has 12 carbon atoms in its chain. Use the general formula of the alkanes to give its molecular formula, and name the family whose general formula is CnH2n. [2]'
Her answer:
studentWorking: The family with general formula CnH2n is the alkenes.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The two general formulae have been swapped in the first line. The alkanes are CnH2n+2, so a 12-carbon alkane has 2 × 12 + 2 = 26 hydrogens, not 24. The second line, which uses CnH2n for the alkenes, is right.
findTheMistake.feedback: One of the two marks. Naming the alkenes is right and stands. The alkane formula needs the +2: double the carbons, then add two, which gives C12H26. The two rules are one character apart, so write both at the top of the page before you start.

findTheMistake.stem:
Dara is asked: 'Explain the term hydrocarbon [2], and give the number of hydrogen atoms in propane [1].'
His answer:
studentWorking: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains hydrogen and carbon.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The propane line is completely right. The definition is missing one word: only. As written it also describes ethanol, which contains hydrogen and carbon and an oxygen as well, and is not a hydrocarbon.
correction: A hydrocarbon is a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only.
findTheMistake.feedback: Two of the three marks: the second mark of the definition and the propane calculation both stand. The mark that goes is the word only, and examiners report it missing every year. Say the two elements, then say only.

findTheMistake.stem:
Ciara is asked: 'Butane boils at −1 °C. State the physical state of butane at room temperature, 20 °C, and explain your answer. [2]'
Her answer:
studentWorking: Butane boils at −1 °C, which is below 20 °C.
So at room temperature butane is a liquid.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The comparison in the first line is right: 20 °C is above butane's boiling point. But above its boiling point a substance has already boiled, so butane is a gas at room temperature, not a liquid.
correction: So at room temperature butane is a gas.
findTheMistake.feedback: One of the two marks: the reason stands, and the state is wrong. Above the boiling point means gas; between the melting and boiling points means liquid. Say the comparison, then read the state off it.

prompts.prompt: Give the four features of a homologous series.
prompts.answer: The same general formula, similar chemical properties, a gradation in physical properties, and successive members differing by a CH2 group.

prompts.prompt: What is a hydrocarbon, and which word in the definition carries a mark of its own?
prompts.answer: A compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only. The word only is the second mark.

prompts.prompt: Give the general formula of the alkanes, and use it for an alkane with 7 carbon atoms.
prompts.answer: CnH2n+2, so 7 carbons give 2 × 7 + 2 = 16 hydrogens: C7H16.

prompts.prompt: Name the first four alkanes in order, and give the molecular formula of each.
prompts.answer: Methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8, butane C4H10.

prompts.prompt: How do you check that a displayed formula you have drawn is right?
prompts.answer: Count the lines at every carbon atom: there must be exactly four, because carbon always forms four covalent bonds.

prompts.prompt: What is the state of the first four alkanes at room temperature, and how do you know?
prompts.answer: All four are gases, because every one of their boiling points is below room temperature, 20 °C.

prompts.prompt: Why do boiling points rise as you go along the alkane family?
prompts.answer: Each member has one more CH2, so the molecules are larger and attract each other more strongly, and more energy is needed to separate them.

prompts.prompt: An alkane has 12 carbon atoms. What is wrong with writing its formula as C12H24+2?
prompts.answer: The arithmetic has not been finished. 2 × 12 + 2 = 26, so the formula is C12H26: a formula has one number after each element.

prompts.prompt: What does a displayed formula show, and how is it different from a molecular formula?
prompts.answer: A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond drawn as a line; a molecular formula only counts the atoms of each element.

prompts.prompt: How many hydrogens would you draw on the middle carbon of any alkane chain, and why?
prompts.answer: Two, because it has already used two of its four bonds joining the carbons on either side of it.
A compound of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

What is the state of methane, ethane, propane and butane at room temperature?

findings.asked: Pick three features of a homologous series, name the family with general formula CnH2n, give the formula of a twelve-carbon alkane, and define a hydrocarbon.
findings.wentWrong: CnH2n was widely taken for the alkanes, or answered with a single compound's name. The twelve-carbon formula was sometimes left with its arithmetic unfinished. The definition of a hydrocarbon lost the word 'only', or called the carbon and hydrogen molecules rather than atoms.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Kept the two general formulae apart, finished the arithmetic before writing the formula, and put the word 'only' into the definition.
findings.rule: Alkanes CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n; a hydrocarbon is hydrogen and carbon only.

findings.asked: The same definition of a hydrocarbon at Higher, with the identification of a homologous series from its general formula.
findings.wentWrong: The definition again lost 'only', and some answers described the carbon and hydrogen as ions.
findings.rule: A hydrocarbon is a compound of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

findings.asked: Read four structures: which are gases, which is an alkane, name a four-carbon alkene, then draw butane.
findings.wentWrong: Few worked out that all four were gases; the structure of butane was drawn poorly; the names were confused with each other.
findings.rule: Count the carbons for the prefix, draw every bond as a line, and compare each boiling point with room temperature.

findings.asked: Organic chemistry across the whole section, including the physical state of propane.
findings.wentWrong: Giving the state of propane defeated many candidates, even with its boiling point in front of them.
findings.rule: Compare the boiling point with room temperature: below it means a gas.

findings.asked: Name and give the formula of organic compounds from their structures, write a general formula, and give a physical state.
findings.wentWrong: Only a few gave the general formula correctly, and only a few gave the physical state; the structure of propene was poorly drawn.
findings.rule: Learn CnH2n+2 for the alkanes, and read a state from the boiling point against room temperature.

insight.ruleToRemember: A homologous series shares a general formula, shows similar chemical properties and a gradation in physical properties, and steps by CH2. Alkanes are CnH2n+2, saturated, and the first four are gases; a hydrocarbon is hydrogen and carbon only. Draw the carbon chain first and add hydrogens until every carbon shows four bonds.
insight.aStarSignal: Moving freely between the name, the molecular formula and the displayed formula of any member, and using the general formula on a chain far beyond the four that are named.
